bio.en:
Alessandro Fiordelmondo is an electronic music performer and researcher in Time-based Media Art and Computer Music.
He studied at the Padova Conservatory of Music, where he received his master's degree with honours in Electronic Music Composition. He studied with Nicola Bernardini, Alberto Novello, and Alvise Vidolin, among others.
Between 2022 and 2024, he carried out a PhD in the History of Art, Film, Audiovisual Media and Music course at the Department of Humanities and Cultural Heritage Studies (DIUM), University of Udine. He was supervised by Cosetta Saba and Sergio Canazza, and his main research topic was the reactivation and preservation of new multimedia art forms.
Since 2019, he has been a research assistant at the Centro di Sonologia Computazionale (CSC), the computer music laboratory of the University of Padua, and Audio Innova, a spinoff of the same university. He has worked on audio/video performances and production, reactivation of multimedia installations, and multimedia software development.
In 2022, he was appointed an expert in Computer Engineering for Music and Multimedia at the Department of Information Engineering (DEI), University of Padua.
He has presented his works and performed at various national and international festivals, including MUSLAB in Mexico City, the SMC—Sound and Music Computing Conference in Stockholm, the Musiques Démesurées festival in Clermont-Ferrand, the Greek National Opera's Sacred Music Festival in Athens, the Biennale Architettura and Biennale Arte in Venice, the CIM—Colloquio di Informatica Musicale in Udine, Sagra Malatestiana in Rimini, and SEAMUS in West Lafayette (Indiana, USA).
bio.it: Alessandro Fiordelmondo è un performer di musica elettronica e ricercatore nell’ambito della Time-based Media Art e della Computer Music. Ha studiato presso il Conservatorio di Musica di Padova, dove ha conseguito il diploma accademico di secondo livello in Composizione di Musica Elettronica con il massimo dei voti e la lode. Ha studiato, tra gli altri, con Alvise Vidolin, Nicola Bernardini e Alberto Novello. Tra il 2022 e il 2024 ha svolto un dottorato di ricerca nel corso di “Storia dell’arte, del cinema, dei media audiovisivi e della musica” presso il Dipartimento di Studi Umanistici e del Patrimonio Culturale (DIUM) dell’Università di Udine, sotto la supervisione di Cosetta Saba e Sergio Canazza. Il suo principale ambito di ricerca è stato la riattivazione e la conservazione delle nuove forme d'arte multimediale. Dal 2019 è assistente di ricerca presso il Centro di Sonologia Computazionale (CSC), laboratorio di informatica musicale dell’Università di Padova, e presso Audio Innova, spin-off dell’Università di Padova. Ha lavorato su performance e produzioni audio/video, sulla riattivazione di installazioni multimediali e sullo sviluppo di applicazioni multimediali. Nel 2022 è stato nominato esperto in “Computer Engineering for Music and Multimedia” presso il Dipartimento di Ingegneria dell’Informazione (DEI) dell’Università di Padova. Ha presentato i suoi lavori e si è esibito in numerosi festival nazionali e internazionali, tra cui MUSLAB a Città del Messico, la SMC—Sound and Music Computing Conference a Stoccolma, il festival Musiques Démesurées di Clermont-Ferrand, il Sacred Music Festival dell’Opera Nazionale Greca di Atene, la Biennale Architettura e la Biannale Arte di Venezia, il CIM—Colloquio di Informatica Musicale di Udine, la Sagra Malatestiana di Rimini e SEAMUS a West Lafayette (Indiana, USA).

exhibition.title: Monitor Yin Yang
exhibition.promotedBy: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, International Trade and Worship – Directorate of Cultural Affairs, Secretariat of Culture of the Nation, and PromArgentina. In collaboration with Estudio Duville and BARRO Gallery

description.primary:
On the occasion of the 61st International Art Exhibition – Venice Biennale, the Argentine Pavilion presents Monitor Yin Yang, a site-specific installation by artist Matías Duville (Buenos Aires, 1974) that transforms the space into a traversable territory built with salt and charcoal. Conceived as an interdisciplinary project, the work expands cdrawing—one of the central languages in Duville’s practice—into a spatial, sonic, and performative experience.
The installation incorporates an original sound composition developed by Centolla Society—a project by Matías Duville with his brother Pablo Duville—in collaboration with Alessandro Fiordelmondo and Alvise Vidolin from the Centro di Sonologia Computazionale (CSC) at the University of Padua. Designed specifically for the pavilion, the sound work unfolds through a multichannel system that creates acoustic paths in dialogue with the architecture and the movement of the audience.
The system integrates real-time environmental data from the city of Venice—such as variations in air quality, suspended particles, and atmospheric conditions—which are translated into sound transformations: density, intensity, texture, and movement. In this way, the installation adds a third component to the elements already present—water (salt) and earth (charcoal): air, introduced as an invisible yet active dimension that becomes part of the work’s sensitive system.
The soundscape does not function as background but as a dynamic layer that modifies the perception of space and constantly evolves. Together with the crunch of footsteps on the salt, it creates a holistic experience where drawing, sound, environmental data, and human presence intertwine in a composition in perpetual transformation.
description.secondary:

exhibition.title: Caravanserraglio

replicas.venue: Aula Rostagni - Dipartimento di Fisica e Astronomia

description.primary:
The sound design for the performance Caravanserraglio was developed by the Centro di Sonologia Computazionale (CSC) of the University of Padua, in collaboration with composer Ardavan Vussoughi and the Sound and Music Processing Lab (SaMPL) of the “Pollini” Conservatory of Padua. The project, coordinated by Professor Sergio Canazza, Director of the CSC, involved the creation of soundscapes and musical material, the design of the live electronics system, and the development of an interactive environment for real-time sound processing.
A central element of the project is the transformation of the astrolabe, an ancient astronomical instrument and a key object in the narrative, into an interactive musical device. The reconstructed astrolabe, designed and developed by Ludovico Di Martino (DEI, University of Padua) and Alessandro Fiordelmondo (CSC), integrates a microcontroller and sensors that track the movements of the object, allowing the actors to generate synthetic sounds and control sound diffusion in real time.
The music, composed by Ardavan Vussoughi and Alessandro Fiordelmondo, was created using recordings of Western acoustic instruments—including clarinet, performed by Matteo Spanio, and various percussion instruments played by Alessandro Cozza—as well as instruments from the Middle Eastern tradition, such as the setar and tar, performed by Darioush Madani. These recordings were combined with computer-generated synthetic sounds.
The resulting sonic materials do more than accompany the stage action. At times they comment on the narrative, while at others they become an integral part of it, acting as an extension of speech that, through sound, shapes the theatrical reality. In this way, the music creates a sonic mirage around the characters, immersing the audience within it.
During the performance, sounds are processed in real time through a dedicated live electronics environment, operated live by Alessandro Fiordelmondo and Mattia Pizzato (SaMPL). The system also enables audio spatialisation through a four-channel loudspeaker setup surrounding the audience, enhancing the immersive experience. The result is a sound environment that integrates speech, music, and technology into a unified expressive dimension.

exhibition.title: Sonificazione Lunare

replicas.event: Paolo De Poli. Il progetto dello smalto tra laboratorio e impresa

description.primary:
Sonificazione Lunare (Lunar Sonification) is a sound installation that uses real-time astronomical data related to the Moon. The work is inspired by the series of artworks by Paolo De Poli based on the distinctive color known as lunar blue, creating a connection between the physical variations of the satellite and the generation of sound.
The parameters considered—including lunar phase, distance from Earth, illumination level, azimuth, altitude, and others—are acquired in real time and mapped to sound synthesis and processing techniques. The installation is distributed across three audio channels, each positioned at a specific location within the exhibition space. Each channel operates as an autonomous entity, driven by different lunar data and contributing to a dynamic and continuously evolving spatialisation of sound.
The aim is to bring the presence of the Moon—the original reference behind lunar blue—into the exhibition space through sound, creating a direct and perceptible connection between astronomical data and the exhibition environment.

exhibition.title: Lezione Concerto: La musica delle macchine: il Disklavier e la generazione artificiale da Bach a oggi

description.primary:
The central element of the event is the Disklavier, an acoustic piano equipped with sensors and electronic actuators that allow its keys and pedals to move automatically, enabling the performance of pieces controlled remotely through MIDI files. Supported by Yamaha Corporation, the choice of the Disklavier was made to allow the AI to perform directly on a physical instrument without a human performer acting as an intermediary, effectively giving it a form of "musical body."
Throughout the event, presentations by Professor Sergio Canazza alternated with listening sessions featuring music generated through artificial intelligence and presented by researcher Alessandro Fiordelmondo, whose work focuses on live electronics and AI-based music systems.
To explore the relationship between composer and AI, composer Ardavan Vossoughi was invited to create a set of original pieces that would serve as the training dataset for a neural network. The model was then used to generate a new composition. For this purpose, Vossoughi composed ten original studies for Disklavier, exploring different compositional possibilities offered by the instrument.
The AI-generated piece was presented both in its original form, as produced by the neural network, and in a revised version subsequently reworked by Vossoughi.

exhibition.title: Echoes of Lamentation: A Vocal Exploration

description.primary: Soprano Niki Lada and electronic music specialist Alessandro Fiordelmondo present a programme of works for voice and electronics that explore emotive vocal expressions, evoking a sense of introspection and emotional depth and creating bridges with the world of sorrow and lament. In Italian composer Salvatore Sciarrino's Due arie marine, extracted from the opera Perseo e Andromeda, traditional instruments are replaced entirely by electronic sounds, creating surreal landscapes that accompany the voice. Their vocal style is stylised and focuses on abstract lyricism, with minimal variation in melody and attention to text intelligibility. The piece Lamento by French composer Franck Bedrossian relies more on the expressive capabilities of the voice itself, augmented by electronic processing. Ethereal voices, whispers, and extended vocal techniques are manipulated in real time to blur the line between acoustic and digital sound. The composition explores a spectrum of emotions from introspection to anguish, through a dynamic interaction between vocal performance and electronic augmentation.

exhibition.title: Perseo e Andromeda

replicas.event: 74th Edition of the Sagra Musicale Malatestiana Festival.

description.primary:
Perseo e Andromeda
One-act opera by Salvatore Sciarrino
for 4 voices and real-time synthesized sounds
Libretto Salvatore Sciarrino, from Moralités légendaires by Jules Laforgue
Editor Casa Ricordi, Milano

The Sagra Musicale Malatestiana presents Perseo e Andromeda by Salvatore Sciarrino in a new production that premiered on 20 October at the Teatro degli Atti in Rimini. The production was conceived by the artists Daniele Spanò and Luca Brinchi, who reimagined the opera as a video and sound installation, highlighting the remarkable dramaturgical potential of Sciarrino’s score.
Perseo e Andromeda is Sciarrino’s first opera and one of the earliest works in the history of musical theatre to completely replace traditional acoustic instruments with electronic sounds generated in real time. The libretto is assembled from fragments of Moralités légendaires, written by Jules Laforgue in the late nineteenth century. In Laforgue’s retelling, Andromeda refuses to accept the destiny of following Perseus, who has killed the monster and freed her from the solitude of her island.

Commissioned by the Stuttgart Opera in 1991, the work was subsequently presented at Teatro alla Scala in Milan and at the Orestiadi Festival in Gibellina. The Rimini production featured a cast of young performers including soprano Eleonora Benetti (Andromeda), mezzo-soprano Arianna Lanci (The Monster), baritone Paolo Leonardi (Perseus I), and bass Giacomo Pieracci (Perseus II). The performance was conducted by Mattia Dattolo, with live electronics by Alessandro Fiordelmondo.
The production was realised in collaboration with the Second-Level Master’s Programme in Vocal Music and Twentieth- and Twenty-First-Century Musical Theatre at the Giuseppe Verdi Conservatory of Ravenna, directed by the renowned soprano Alda Caiello.

Following a classical concert in which the Haydn Orchestra of Bolzano and Trento, conducted by Ottavio Dantone, will perform Franz Joseph Haydn’s Symphony No. 95 in C minor, Hoboken I/95, and Ludwig van Beethoven’s Symphony No. 4 in B-flat major, Op. 60, the evening will continue with AI Ludwig van…?, a composition by Alvise Vidolin in collaboration with Alessandro Fiordelmondo.

description.primary: The work is a study on spatialisation techniques and consists of nine stereophonic tracks and fifteen statuses. The horizontal structure is given by the succession of statuses representing different perspectives of a sound sculpture (never presented in its entirety). Like a succession of images that, through different perspectives, show a set of details of a marble sculpture. Similarly, the statuses consist of a vertical layering of sound elements (one per track) frozen in time and determining the sound sculpture from certain listening points. The performer’s function is to experience each sound status through diffusion and spatialisation in space (spatialisation as a form of augmented listening). The performer must choose the spatial interpretation of each status, the spatialisation strategy to be applied and the sound system in which to perform the piece.

exhibition.title: DISALLINEATO

description.primary:
Disallineato is a critically acclaimed theatrical production by the Franco-Algerian author Hakim Djaziri and produced by the Rome-based company MAGMA06. It stars actor Nour Zrafi under the direction of Valentina Favella.
The show is a intimate reflection on cultural belonging, exile, identity loss, and extremism. It explores the life of an immigrant torn between the protective warmth of his upbringing, the rise of fundamentalism in Algeria, and the pull of extremist ideologies. Djaziri contrasts the protagonist's path with his own, highlighting how his ability to distance himself from the ideology of hate made all the difference.
The MAGMA06's production is notable for its technical setup: The audio design features a human-machine interface developed in collaboration with Audio Innova, a spin-off of the University of Padua.
Creative Team: Features voice-over work by Christian Iansante and Mariagrazia Pompei (who founded MAGMA06)

author: Nicola Bernardini

publication.title: Inside Andrea Molino's La vérité, pas toute: The Creation of Swarm Sounds
publication.abstract:
The paper is a technical description of a specific component of La Vérité, pas toute, a large scale dense and theatrically engaging work by Italian composer Andrea Molino.
Specifically, it outlines the tools and techniques developed to digitally create the “sonic swarms” that are called for in the score. Such swarms are generated, controlled and spatialized in real time and, as such, they present an interesting use case for live electronics environments.

author: Alessandro Russo
Alessandro Fiordelmondo
Andrea Franceschini
Sergio Canazza
publication.title: Restoration and reactivation approaches in computer music and time-based media art
publication.abstract: This paper presents the work carried out by the Centro di Sonologia Computazionale (CSC) of the University of Padua, regarding the reactivation and preservation of time-based media artworks, including computer music, live electronics, performances, and multimedia art installations. During the last few years, the CSC has been developing a specific approach for archiving, documenting, and reactivating time-based media artworks, which led to the definition of the Multilevel Dynamic Preservation (MDP) model. Through in-depth analysis, various approaches are examined in the reactivation of several case studies, including digitisation, restoration, migration, and virtualisation of the artworks. The selected case studies involve various forms of art expression, such as video art, computer music, expanded cinema, and interactive performance. This contribution offers a comprehensive overview of the challenges encountered in the process of reactivating and preserving multimedia art, investigating the possible solutions offered by new technologies in preserving, digitising and virtualizing some of its forms, such as multimedia installations, expanded cinema, and video art performances.

author: Alessandro Fiordelmondo
Matteo Spanio
Patricia Cadavid
Xinran Chen
Sergio Canazza
Raul Masu
publication.title: Towards a Repository Template for Music Technology Research
publication.abstract:
Documenting and sharing research output is essential to construct the critical discourse on new music technology. Documentation feeds the knowledge and the values with which to evaluate and discuss current achievements and musical creations as well as to plan for the future. Besides publishing our research in conferences and journals, sharing research materials and outcomes like software, hardware, instruments, and datasets is important. This allows others to use the latest technology and improve it. For this purpose, the repository is increasingly commonly used by researchers and artists to store and share their works. However, creating repositories does not follow a clear and organised structure like the one we find, for example, in papers. The heterogeneity of repositories makes it hard to use both practically and for analysis. Although the variety and differences of research products in the field of new musical technologies are obvious, we believe that defining repositories with common guidelines could significantly improve the critical discourse in this area. This issue has been discussed at the NIME conference through workshops and papers. In this article, we want to continue this discussion and propose a flexible repository template to organise and present research materials and outcomes in the field of musical technologies research.
The article provides a short and focused review of how repositories are currently used at the NIME conference, with special attention to the platforms used. Based on this study, we introduce a repository template that will be applied to case studies. We hope this proposal will encourage further discussion and advancement on this issue and, at the same time, support and facilitate the creation of new repositories.
publication.booktitle: Proceedings of the International Conference on New Interfaces for Musical Expression

author: Anna Zuccante
Alessandro Fiordelmondo
Pierluigi Bontempi
Sergio Canazza
publication.title: A Signal-Processing-Based Simulation System for High-End Stereo Headsets
publication.abstract: In recent years, headphones have become increasingly popular worldwide. There are numerous models on the market today, varying in technical characteristics and offering different listening experiences. This article presents an application for simulating the sound response of specific headphone models by physically wearing others. In the future, for example, this application could help to guide people who already own a pair of headphones during the decision-making process of purchasing a new headphone model. However, the potential fields of application are much broader. An in-depth study of digital signal processing was carried out with the implementation of a computational model. Prior to this, an analysis was performed on impulse response measurements of specific headphones, which allowed for a better understanding of the behavior of each set of headphones. Finally, an evaluation of the entire system was conducted through a listening test. The analysis of the results showed that the software works reasonably well in replicating the target headphones. We hope that this work will stimulate further efforts in the same direction.

author: Alessandro Fiordelmondo
Giada Zuccolo
Sergio Canazza
Raul Masu
publication.title: Longevity in NIME research: a case study using time-based media art preservation models
publication.abstract: This paper presents the reactivation of Soundrise, an interactive multimedia application for deaf children, as a case study to demonstrate the application of time-based media art preservation and reactivation strategies in NIMEs. Drawing upon the Multilevel Dynamic Preservation (MDP) model and the Digital Preservation Object (DPO), structured frameworks designed to comprehensively document time-based media art across different levels of information and iterative processes, this article introduces a novel decision-making process for reactivating NIMEs, outlined in five steps: Collection, Assessment, (re)Design, Implementation, and Archiving. Through an exploration of the Soundrise reactivation, the article elaborates on each step of the proposed reactivation process, illustrating the application of the DPO and MDP model to ensure the preservation of the application. From the analysis of the previous iterations of the application, we also provide design reflections on obsolescence and longevity. By aligning our work with recent NIME literature on documentation and reuse, we aim to offer insights on how to preserve, reuse, or maintain and document research.
publication.booktitle: Proceedings of the International Conference on New Interfaces for Musical Expression

author: Alessandro Fiordelmondo
Sergio Canazza
Niccolò Pretto
publication.title: Reactivating and Preserving Interactive Multimedia Artworks: An Analog Performance from the Seventies
publication.abstract:
Interactive multimedia art shows a complex nature as it is time- and process-based, interconnected with technology, derived by the participation of several authors (artists, technicians, performers, to name a few) and an audience, and it is strongly tied to the moment and space of the original exhibition. These characteristics make the preservation of these artworks a multifaceted process. Building on the foundations developed since the 2000s by international projects focused on preserving and restoring these new art forms, the paper proposes an original model for achieving dynamic preservation, called “the multilevel preservation model”. Since it is no longer possible to guarantee physical integrity for interactive multimedia artworks, dynamic preservation involves recording all the changes that occur to display the artworks in the future. In other words, it makes it possible to record the dynamic authenticity of artworks. The model proposes two fundamental properties: multiple layering, which allows to handle different levels of information about the artwork; multiple belongingness, which allows to represent the dynamic authenticity of the artwork at the archival level and achieving dynamic preservation.
The paper demonstrates the high-level implementation of the model by presenting a case study: the reactivation and preservation of an analog video art performance from the 1970s. This case study proposes an interesting real scenario for testing the model, as the reactivation process involved the migration of the entire analog technological apparatus of the artwork into the digital domain.

author: Michael Castronuovo
Alessandro Fiordelmondo
Cosetta Saba
publication.title: Toward a System of Visual Classification, Analysis and Recognition of Performance-Based Moving Images in the Artistic Field
publication.abstract: This paper proposes a research program focused on the design of a model for the recognition, analysis and classification of video art works and documentations based on their semiotic aspects and audiovisual content. Focusing on a corpus of art cinema, video art, and performance art, the theoretical framework involves bringing together semiotics, film studies, visual studies, and performance studies with the innovative technologies of computer vision and artificial intelligence. The aim is to analyze the performance aspect to interpret contextual references and cultural constructs recorded in artistic contexts, contributing to the classification and analysis of video art works with complex semiotic characteristics. Underlying the conceptual framework is the simultaneous use of a set of technologies, such as pose estimation, facial recognition, object recognition, motion analysis, audio analysis, and natural language processing, to improve recognition accuracy and create a large set of labeled audiovisual data. In addition, the authors propose a prototype application to explore the primary challenges of such a research project.

author: Alessandro Fiordelmondo
Alessandro Russo
Mattia Pizzato
Luca Zecchinato
Sergio Canazza
publication.title: A multilevel dynamic model for documenting, reactivating and preserving interactive multimedia art
publication.abstract:
During the last years, preservation of interactive multimedia artworks has become a growing research field. In fact, the role played by multimedia within the performing arts has become more and more important, thanks to the development of new technologies. Nevertheless, technologies inevitably face issues related to obsolescence of devices, operating systems etc.
In dealing with interactive multimedia artworks, consolidated preservation strategies are inadequate, because they don't cover the complex relations between analogue and digital components that can be used for the realization of the artwork.
Therefore, there is the need to develop a preservation model capable of preserving analogue and digital components, as well as the experience and the human interaction, in compliance with the intent of the artist. This work presents the multilevel dynamic preservation (MDP) model, developed at the Centro di Sonologia Computazionale (CSC) of the Department of Information Engineering of the University of Padova.
In the last part of this work, the proposed model is applied to the reactivation of the Il caos delle sfere, a 1999 installation by Italian composer Carlo De Pirro. The overall reactivation process of the artwork aimed at preserving its identity, rather than simply replicating the original performance. For this purpose, before proceeding with the reactivation of the artwork, several approaches were investigated, in order to choose the more suitable one.
Given the complexity of the artwork, it has been chosen to proceed with a hybrid approach, since a technology migration was necessary for the communication node, while for other components (i.e. the pinball and the Disklavier piano) it was possible to proceed with a ”purist” approach. The reactivation of the artwork produced new documentation, that filled the gap in the existing one. In fact, the documentation process covers a central role in the proposed model, both for preserving and reactivating the artwork

publication.abstract: Il "controller pittorico" permette di controllare la sintesi sonora dipingendo. Lo strumento consiste in una tavola il cui piano di lavoro è dotato di sensori che comunicano con un software musicale la scelta cromatica e la gestualità dell’artista tramite la conduttività elettrica dell'acqua e della grafite. Colori e segni vengono tradotti musicalmente in tempo reale

author: Alberto Novello
Alessandro Fiordelmondo
Arcangelo Di Donato
publication.title: PhOS: a photo-sensitive gestural surface
publication.abstract: We present PhOS: a system that uses incident light intensity to control music parameters and sound synthesis. It is a transparent surface with 16 sensors each measuring ambient light, red, green and blue intensity values. The sensors are spaced on a 4x4 grid, making gestural control quite intuitive for the user, through the creation of light trajectories on the surface. Given its simplicity, with the direct translation of light into sound, and the ubiquitous distribution of light-emitting devices such as inexpensive bike lights and mobile phone flash lights, it can be used in multiple occasions from live performances to sound installations.
